localBiteReport: The most current dated report available from Half Hitch (Destin Fishing Report 9-28-26, roughly 11 days old as of today) confirms the site is actively posting, though its full bay-fishing content was not retrievable via search. From captainexperiences.com's Choctawhatchee Bay page — updated within the past week with guide check-ins coinciding with the start of the Destin Fishing Rodeo — local Fort Walton Beach-area guides are reporting that redfish and speckled trout are active in the bayous, with the inshore bite described as heating up heading into October. Water temperature at this location is 83°F. The mullet run, which typically fires up the fall redfish bite along grass edges and river mouths in the Choctawhatchee system, is the key seasonal driver right now, and moving-tide windows around bay structure (bridges, dock lights, grass flats) are the most reliable setups for reds and trout.
